Mutation B (agentId alone) -> 1 red; mutation C (sidechain alone) -> 2 red. Both halves of the conjunct are load-bearing.

h3-spine-rail-guard.title: The _spine_rail is None guard was carried to the new call site
h3-spine-rail-guard.imperative: Confirm moving binding_key out to handle_post_tool_use carried the guard, and that a sibling-import failure produces a visible skip rather than an exception swallowed into silence.
h3-spine-rail-guard.finding: CARRIED, and it is a visible skip rather than a swallowed exception. The guard is 'if _spine_rail is None: return None' as the first statement of _binding_key (line 223), and _binding_key deliberately carries no try/except of its own - so a missing guard would surface as a raised AttributeError rather than being absorbed by handle_post_tool_use's outer except. I verified this directly rather than through their test: with gw._spine_rail set to None, _binding_key({'session_id':'s1'}) and _binding_key({'session_id':'s1','agent_id':...}) both return None without raising, and the full handler returns {} having written no gauge and no sidecar. resolve_gauge_path keeps its own independent 'if _spine_rail is None or not binding_key' guard (line 248), so the guard was duplicated to the new call site, not moved away from the old one.

h4-duration-placement.title: Second opinion: duration field on the dispatched-agent path only
h4-duration-placement.imperative: Judge whether recording identity_resolution_ms only on the dispatched-agent record is the right reading of 'records its own duration in the gauge write'. Say what you think.
h4-duration-placement.finding: SECOND OPINION: I agree with the implementer, and I would not accept the alternative. 'Records its own duration in the gauge write' has to mean 'records it when there was an identity to resolve' - a top-level agent resolves no identity (no derivation, no existence check, just the bare session_id), so a top-level duration field would report the cost of nothing. It is also forced: the pre-existing test_golden_fixture_produces_well_formed_record pins the record to exactly four keys and the byte-identical constraint forbids editing it, so the only reading that survives all three requirements is the one taken. The measurement itself is real, not a constant - I confirmed test_identity_resolution_duration_tracks_a_deliberately_slowed_step injects a 30ms sleep into spine_rail.binding_key and requires slow >= 25.0 AND slow > fast + 20.0, which a hardcoded value or a timer around the wrong span both fail. My own harness read 0.082ms against the 100ms budget. Two minor observations, neither blocking: the value is written unrounded (0.08230004459619522) where ~4 decimals would carry the same information, and the reasoning is written at the code site as the handoff wanted.

h5-allowlist-denylist.title: Second opinion: spine_rail denylist vs this module's allowlist divergence
h5-allowlist-denylist.imperative: Confirm the characterization - an id like a:b gets a binding written by spine_rail that this module never resolves, an orphaned dict entry with NO filesystem hazard - and confirm the divergence carries a comment at the code site.
h5-allowlist-denylist.finding: CHARACTERIZATION CONFIRMED, INCLUDING 'no filesystem hazard'. I traced every use of the binding key in spine_rail.py: it appears only as a dict key - binding[key][abs_spine_path] on claim (line 434-441), del binding[key] on release (455), and a startswith prefix comparison in session_view (207). It is never interpolated into a path, opened, or joined. So an id like 'a:b' produces binding['s1#a:b'], which gauge_writer_hook._binding_key refuses to compose and therefore never resolves: an orphaned dict entry, cleared by a clean release (same key) and surviving only a crash. No filesystem hazard - confirmed at source, not accepted. The divergence DOES carry a comment at the code site: gauge_writer_hook.py lines 161-171, which names the denylist, names the three characters it still admits (':', '*', '?'), and states why this module needs a stricter rule (it interpolates agent_id into agent-{id}.jsonl on a Windows filesystem, spine_rail does not). Their test compares the two functions in one assertion rather than describing the gap, so the divergence cannot drift silently. The durable fix - one shared allowlist in spine_rail - is correctly filed as a triage candidate rather than done under a closed exclusion.
